editorNote: Today: a quiet intrusion campaign against firewall management, an Exchange alternative, a DNS resolver leaving France, and two items on how far to trust models, plus an unverified trading claim.

stories.headline: GreyNoise tracks an intrusion campaign that reached Check Point management servers at 22 or more organizations
stories.summary: GreyNoise says an unattributed campaign, tracked as GT13, chained a Rejetto HFS cookie-forgery flaw with a Check Point SmartConsole authentication bypass, with data saved from 24 management servers. Its report puts activity between early October and Nov. 2.
stories.whyItMatters: Victims span financial services, energy and government across 17 countries, and the attacker blocked rivals from its relay.

sourceLinks.title: Cyberattack campaign compromising Check Point servers across 22 organizations (GreyNoise)

stories.headline: Stalwart 1.2.0 speaks Exchange's protocols, so Outlook and phone mail apps can point at it
stories.summary: Stalwart's open-source Community edition now implements MAPI over HTTP, EWS, ActiveSync and Autodiscover, and a Vandelay tool imports from on-premises Exchange and Microsoft 365. Public folders, archive mailboxes and NTLM/Kerberos sign-in are not supported.
stories.whyItMatters: Self-hosters get a documented route off Exchange without changing every client, with the Exchange code off by default behind a Cargo feature.

sourceLinks.title: Stalwart is now a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange

stories.headline: Quad9 goes dark for French users today, 09:00 Paris time, after court-backed piracy-blocking demands
stories.summary: Quad9 said it would refuse all queries from French users from Nov. 24 at 09:00 CET, citing beIN's blocking demands, French court rulings and fines. It admits geoIP identification will over- and under-block.
stories.whyItMatters: A previously announced deadline has arrived: a public resolver is leaving a country rather than apply content blocking.

stories.headline: A blogger argues LLM agents serve their parent companies, and wants a homelab model instead
stories.summary: Michael Harley says his Claude Code skill for finding an artist's Bandcamp page broke after Bandcamp added a search challenge, and that Claude declined to help get around it while the same skill could still fetch the song from YouTube. He concludes he wants a model he runs himself.
stories.whyItMatters: This is one user's account, but it is a concrete case of vendor policy shaping what a personal tool will do.

sourceLinks.title: LLM agents work for their parent companies, not for you

stories.headline: Paper: language models barely notice their own reasoning errors, but respond to injected doubt
stories.summary: Across four open-weight 7B–14B-class models on math tasks, verbalized confidence at a model's first error stayed at 95.1–99.9%. Inserting a low-confidence tag at the error step improved correction by 3.7 to 22.5 points, while injecting doubt into correct steps cut solve rates by up to 22.8 points.
stories.whyItMatters: The author's conclusion is that self-correction is limited by detecting errors in the moment, not by fixing them.

sourceLinks.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ (arXiv)

stories.headline: A blog post alleges a suspicious Polymarket bet before Jensen Huang's reinstatement; the evidence is circumstantial
stories.summary: The post says wallet 'ljhggk' bought about 71,518 shares at $0.065 (about $4,649) on a Huang-returns-by-year-end contract before Trump's Truth Social post and Nvidia's announcement, for a roughly $71,518 payout. The author concedes the wallet owner and funding source are unknown, and the post has internal inconsistencies.
stories.whyItMatters: A follow-up to Nvidia's reinstatement: an unverified insider-trading claim from an author who built a monitoring tool.

sourceLinks.title: Investigation of Polymarket Insider Trading on the Reinstatement of Jensen Huang
